                        BROWN BRIGGS RANCH’S REPLY BRIEF

       COMES NOW, Brown Briggs Ranch LLC (“Brown Briggs Ranch/Intervenor”) and

respectfully submits this Reply Brief following the Hearing on the Merits in the above referenced

docket, pursuant to the applicable SOAH order.

I.     INTRODUCTION
       Applicants repeatedly recognize that multiple filed routes are constructible, satisfy the

Project's engineering requirements, and remain available for Commission consideration. Because

multiple viable routing options exist, the Commission should select the route that best balances

the statutory routing factors while minimizing unnecessary impacts to affected landowners. Which

said route does not include segments G31 and G9.

       The record demonstrates that routing the Project through Brown Briggs Ranch by utilizing

Segments G31 or G9 would impose substantial and permanent impacts that can be avoided through
 the selection of another available route. Accordingly, the Commission should decline to select any

route utilizing segments G31 and G9.

II.      APPLICANTS CONFIRM THAT MULTIPLE ROUTES ARE AVAILABLE TO

         THE COMMISSION


         Applicants repeatedly state that all filed routes are technically feasible and satisfy the

Project's engineering objectives. That recognition shifts the Commission's inquiry from whether

the Project can be built to which available route best satisfies the statutory routing factors.

         Applicants also recognize that no single routing factor is dispositive and that the

Commission must balance all relevant considerations. The Commission is not required to select a

route simply because it is constructible. Rather, it should evaluate the comparative impacts of the

available routes and select the route that best balances the statutory routing factors.

         That balancing requires meaningful consideration of the permanent impacts imposed upon

individual properties where reasonable alternatives exist. The Commission need not select a route

that unnecessarily burdens Brown Briggs Ranch simply because that route is technically feasible.

For Brown Briggs Ranch, the statutory balancing weighs against the selection of Segments G31

or G9.

III.     THE RECORD ESTABLISHES G31 AND G9 WOULD IMPOSE UNNECESSARY

         IMPACTS ON BROWN BRIGGS RANCH

         The evidence presented by Brown Briggs Ranch establishes that routing the transmission

line through the ranch would have consequences extending well beyond the installation of

transmission structures. The proposed route would interfere with residences on the property,

agricultural operations, including the family's orchard and apiaries, affect access to Berry Creek

and portions of the ranch, fragment wildlife habitat, and diminish the property's long-established
 conservation and stewardship efforts. These impacts are unique to the way Brown Briggs Ranch

is owned, managed, and used. They directly implicate several of the routing considerations

identified in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values, environmental integrity, and the use

and enjoyment of private property.

       The evidence also demonstrates that Brown Briggs Ranch is uniquely affected by the

concentration of nearby infrastructure, including the Matterhorn Express Pipeline, the planned

Eiger Pipeline, the Firefly Aerospace facility, and nearby helicopter operations. These cumulative

impacts further distinguish Brown Briggs Ranch from other affected properties and reinforce that

the Commission can achieve the Project's objectives through alternative route combinations that

avoid these unnecessary burdens.

       Applicants have not demonstrated why routing through Brown Briggs Ranch is preferable

to other available routes that would accomplish the Project's purpose while avoiding these impacts.

Instead, Applicants acknowledge that alternative route combinations remain available and

preferred namely, routes 894 and 487 that do not include segments G31 and G9 for the

Commission’s consideration. Where reasonable alternatives exist, the Commission should avoid

imposing permanent and unnecessary burdens upon a single property owner.

IV.    THE STATUTORY BALANCING FACTORS FAVOR A ROUTE THAT AVOIDS

       BROWN BRIGGS RANCH

       PURA § 37.056(c) requires the Commission to balance numerous considerations rather

than elevate any single factor above all others. Nothing in the record demonstrates that selecting

Segments G31 or G9 provides a corresponding engineering or reliability benefit that outweighs

the significant property-specific impacts established by the evidence. Conversely, the evidence

demonstrates that selecting a route avoiding Segments G31 and G9 would continue to satisfy the
 Project's engineering and reliability objectives while reducing unnecessary impacts to an actively

managed family ranch, its agricultural operations, natural resources, and long-established

stewardship efforts. The statutory balancing therefore favors selection of a route that avoids

imposing these unnecessary burdens.

V.     CONCLUSION

       Brown Briggs Ranch respectfully requests that the Commission reject any route utilizing

Segments G31 or G9 and instead approve a route that satisfies the Project's objectives while

avoiding the unnecessary impacts established by the record.
